custom_logic_notes: This is a market-making spreader for FORTS (Russian derivatives exchange). Core logic: 1) On each book event, delete pending orders that are no longer at best bid/offer or need to be moved. 2) If holding a position with no pending orders, place a closing limit order (opposite side) at 2x volume (implies flipping from long to short or vice versa with double size). 3) If flat with no pending orders and spread >= SpreadToPutOrders*minStep, place both a Sell Limit at Ask-minStep and a Buy Limit at Bid+minStep to capture the spread. 4) isBestBidOrOfferOnlyMy checks if our pending order is the only order at the best price level AND there is a gap > minStep to the next level - if so, the order is deleted (we are alone at best price, unfavorable). 5) needMove checks if the pending order price has drifted more than minStep from current Bid/Ask - if so, delete and re-place. 6) calcDiff checks for a price gap > minStep between adjacent order book levels at the best price.
python_conversion_notes: This EA is fundamentally incompatible with standard Python backtesting frameworks. Reasons: 1) OnBookEvent requires L2 order book data (MarketBookGet), which most Python backtesting frameworks do not support. 2) The logic dynamically manages pending limit orders based on real-time order book state - scanning for own orders at best bid/offer, checking volume at price levels, detecting gaps between book levels. 3) ORDER_FILLING_RETURN is exchange-specific (FORTS) and allows partial fills with remaining quantity staying as a limit order. 4) The 2x volume closing mechanism implies a position-flipping strategy. 5) To convert, you would need a custom framework supporting L2 data replay, order book state tracking, and pending order management with move/cancel logic. A simplified version could work with just spread monitoring + limit order placement, but the order-book-aware order management (isBestBidOrOfferOnlyMy, needMove, calcDiff) would be lost.
